name: Vanuatu
summary: Red over green divided by a black-edged yellow horizontal Y, with a black triangle at the hoist bearing a curled boar's tusk and two crossed namele fern leaves. Adopted in 1980 for independence from the Anglo-French condominium of the New Hebrides.
origin: The colours come from the Vanua'aku Pati, which led the independence movement. Kalontas Malon's design was adopted on 18 February 1980, ahead of independence on 30 July 1980.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The blood of boars and of the people.

colors.name: Yellow
colors.meaning: The light of Christianity spreading through the islands.

symbols.name: Boar's tusk
symbols.description: A curled tusk in the black triangle.
symbols.meaning: Prosperity; tusked boars are a traditional sign of wealth.

symbols.name: Namele leaves
symbols.description: Two crossed fern leaves inside the tusk.
symbols.meaning: Peace; their 39 fronds represent the 39 members of the first parliament.

symbols.name: Yellow Y
symbols.meaning: The shape of the island chain and the light of the Gospel.

facts: Before 1980 the islands were jointly ruled by Britain and France as the New Hebrides.
South Africa's flag also uses a horizontal Y shape.
Its designer was an art student when he won the competition.
clues: Red and green divided by a yellow Y, with a boar's tusk and fern leaves in a black triangle.
Its fern fronds number the members of the first parliament.
Its country was once ruled jointly by two European powers.
